import framebuf
w, h = 240, 320
# MONO_HMSB packs 8px/byte, each row padded UP to a whole byte -- ceil(w/8)
# is the real per-row byte count. MONO_HMSB specifically, NOT MONO_VLSB
# (display_i2c's own OLED convention, vertical byte columns -- wrong
# orientation for this node's row-by-row streaming) or MONO_HLSB (same
# 8px/byte row orientation as MONO_HMSB, but the OPPOSITE bit order --
# see display-spi.ts's header for why MONO_HMSB was picked).
stride = (w + 7) // 8
buf = bytearray(stride * h)
fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, h, framebuf.MONO_HMSB)
# Only 2 palette indices read in mono mode: 0 black, 1 white (the
# default palette's own first two entries) -- palette property left
# unset on purpose, same as the gs4/gs2 test flows.
fb.fill(0)
fb.text('MONO 240x320', 8, 8, 1)
fb.rect(20, 40, w - 40, 200, 1)
fb.ellipse(120, 260, 50, 50, 1, True)
msg['payload'] = bytes(buf)
return msg
